items.title: Uttarakhand SIR: Who is targeting Muslim voters?
items.summary: A Newslaundry investigation into the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process in Uttarakhand has revealed a deeply concerning pattern. Numerous applications were filed to remove the names of Muslim voters from the electoral rolls. Many of the individuals listed as applicants in these filings are associated with the BJP. Following the discovery of such cases, more questions arose. Were these objections filed en masse without adhering to the rules? And if so, what action did the Election Commission take? The findings go further still. Some of the individuals in whose names these objections were filed later submitted affidavits stating that they had never filed them in the first place. They alleged that their names, EPIC numbers, and signatures had been fraudulently used. Did the Election Commission initiate any FIR or criminal proceedings following these complaints? What exactly is transpiring in Uttarakhand under the guise of the SIR? Who is behind these applications to remove names of Muslim voters? And why is the role of the Election Commission coming under scrutiny? Watch this video. Our new project visits the landscape described in Vande Mataram as it stand

items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday restrained Kwick Living, which sells products under the Beco brand, from continuing its 'War on What’s Hidden' advertising campaign targeting Hindustan Unilever Limited’s Surf Excel and Vim products. [HUL v. Kwick Living] Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani held that while comparative advertising may place a rival’s product in an unfavourable light, it crosses the legal line when the overall message is false, misleading or deceptive. The Court found that Beco had prima facie failed to establish the truth of the message conveyed by its campaign. “ Just because a comparative advertisement is derisive or denigrating or unflattering of the competitor’s product or service does not necessarily imply that it amounts to disparagement in law. ” The Court explained that truthful but unfavourable comparison cannot become actionable merely because the competitor considers it disparaging. For a comparative advertisement to amount to disparagement in law, it must involve falsehood, misrepresentation or deception that causes injury to the competitor’s intellectual property or reputation, it said. The Karnataka Cabinet has approved the reintroduction of student union elections, which were banned in 1989-90 following a series of violent incidents and clashes in educational institutions during the tenure of then Chief Minister Veerendra Patil. The elections, however, will not be mandatory. items.title: Supreme Court to examine plea challenging closure of Delhi metro stations during CJP protests

Union of India and Ors]. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing the plea questioning whether the executive can direct the closure of metro stations, thereby restricting public access to a public utility, without a specific statutory provision or formal order. Taking note of the submissions, Justice Bagchi observed that courts ordinarily defer to the executive on law-and-order issues, but can intervene where executive discretion is exercised disproportionately. “The concept of SOP is actually a mirage. When it comes to a law and order question, courts have deferred to the executive authority. It is only in cases when it becomes disproportionate, as you indicated, that courts step in. The High Court’s approval was required in view of the apex court’s 2021 judgment in the Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay case, which mandates strict judicial scrutiny to curb the misuse of executive power in dropping prosecutions against lawmakers. Today, the top court said that none of the cases involving the lawmakers in Himachal Pradesh disclosed the commission of grave or heinous crimes.
